facts.fact: Actual source precedence is L2, then unclaimed mirror, then READ. GPU hits never enter this claim path.
The comment at598-599 saying ring before L2 is stale; executable cpp633-660 is authoritative. Offline stage leaves runtime/header untouched.

Mirror hit preserves expert mapping and cursor, releases claim after recording source H2D event, and adds expert to GPU; GPU/mirror duplication is permitted. L2 hits likewise do not clear mirror mappings.
Each occupied GPU overwrite attempts writeback. Scan from cursor takes first event-ready/unclaimed ring slot; no empty-slot, GPU-covered or L2-covered preference. Cursor advances at reservation.

Publication follows event record, replaces target and invalidates same-expert mappings elsewhere. Abort releases reservation only; cursor and old mapping are not explicitly rolled back. Do not assume transaction semantics or payload rollback on CUDA errors.
Task claims all entries before reads/commits; cross-task worker order is unknown. Host completion barrier closes tasks without being a new CUDA synchronization.

Each MoE forward synchronizes router D2H before planning; true T=1 decode therefore starts after prior stream events. Prefill subchunks within one forward carry live residency and use worker barriers, not a new stream drain between subchunks.

Ring initialization/clearing belongs to Init/Free, not request/phase transition. Captured snapshots expose ring IDs/cursor and GPU/L2 membership. Current observer retains candidate aggregates/direct-loss witnesses, not a full ring lifecycle.

hypothesis: GPU/L2-covered ring entries may occupy capacity while sole lower-cache copies are replaced. Endpoint redundancy and subsequent GPU victim reuse are opportunities, not proof of overwrite or saved READ.
identifiable_offline: Fixed successful GPU plan miss/victim sets from existing exact GPU core, with full endpoints and prefix counts checked by runner.
Possible support from actual decode-entry mirrors union all strictly earlier occupied GPU victims; never last-K trim.
Latest prior victim plan gap i-j and strictly intervening victim count summed only over j<r<i; entry-only support gets no synthetic eviction date.
Independent first future GPU eviction and first GPU miss of each entry mirror, with end-of255 censoring.
Conservative common-miss candidate count intervals from observed C and separately capped common/only/total support.
not_identifiable: Actual per-plan ring membership, claim availability, reserve target alternatives, event-query/publication order, skip history and complete mirror lifetime.
Unique lower-cache baseline replay from routes and phase endpoints.
Causal history decomposition, actual hypothetical READ savings or speed benefit; overlap alone cannot select a policy.
limits: Plan0/1miss can be conditionally advanced from a fully known drained entry; multi-miss interleavings prevent general exact history reconstruction.
No old16/new8 pooling. No current-plan victims as current entry support. No claim about physical IO, exclusive waits, performance acceptance or54GB.
